record.what_it_does: Financial data API connecting bank accounts: transactions, balances, identity, payments, income verification.
record.auth_notes: Core API uses a client_id and secret, sent in the body or as PLAID-CLIENT-ID and PLAID-SECRET headers. Each end user's bank link yields an access_token, which is stored per Item. OAuth client_credentials applies only to the Dashboard MCP server. Plaid is not an OAuth provider for third-party apps in the usual sense.
record.access_notes: Sandbox keys are free on Dashboard signup. Production requires applying for Production access, and the billing page says "To view pricing, apply for Production access." A free Trial plan allows 10 Production Items, for US/Canada teams created on or after 2026-04-15. Pay-as-you-go is also available. EU/UK customers are limited to Custom plans. Whether the application is reviewed is unclear.
record.api_breadth_notes: Many products: Auth, Transactions, Balance, Identity, Assets, Investments, Liabilities, Income, Transfer, Link, and others. This is well over 50 endpoints. I did not count them.
record.mcp_notes: Dashboard MCP at https://api.dashboard.plaid.com/mcp/ (streamable HTTP, OAuth bearer with the mcp:dashboard scope, Production only). It targets Dashboard and developer tasks, not end-user financial data. Plaid also has a local MCP server in its AI coding toolkit.
record.blocker_notes: Sandbox is self-serve. Live bank data needs Production approval, and each end user must go through Plaid Link. Production credentials belong to the developer team, so a multi-tenant toolkit needs customers to bring their own client_id and secret.
